outcome: proportion of total morphine milligram equivalents (MMEs) dispensed after surgery attributed to each procedure type
cohort: Over 1 million adults aged 18-64 years who underwent major surgical procedures and had private or public health insurance in the United States between December 1, 2020, and November 30, 2021
finding: Cesarean delivery accounted for the largest proportion of opioids dispensed after surgery among individuals aged 18-44 years, while orthopedic procedures accounted for the majority of opioid prescriptions in those aged 45-64 years.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery accounted for the largest proportion (19.4%) of total MMEs dispensed after surgery among individuals aged 18 to 44 years.
